memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The Lord God made garments of skin for Adam and his wife and clothed them. — Gen 3:21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
It is easy to read past this verse quickly, but slow down and look at it — there is deep tenderness here. Adam and Eve had tried to cover their own shame with fig leaves (Gen 3:7), flimsy and quickly withering. Now God Himself steps in and does what they could not. He makes proper garments, and He clothes them with His own hands.

Notice the cost hidden in this. These garments were "of skin" — which means an animal had to die. For the first time in the story, blood is shed. Something innocent gives up its life so that the guilty can be covered. Their homemade fig leaves are set aside, and God provides a covering that actually lasts, but only through death.

We should be careful not to over-read the detail, yet the pattern here runs right through the whole Bible. Human effort cannot deal with our shame; only a covering God provides, at the cost of life, will do. Here in Eden is the faint first shadow of it.

Dear friend, do you see the grace? Even as Adam and Eve are being sent out from the garden, God is caring for them, clothing them, providing what they cannot provide for themselves. And this points us forward to the greatest covering of all — when the Lamb of God shed His own blood so that we might be clothed in His righteousness (2 Cor 5:21). We cannot cover ourselves. But God, in Christ, has covered us completely.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. In what ways do you still try to cover your shame with "fig leaves" of your own making?
2. How does it move you that God clothes His children rather than leaving them exposed?
3. What does it mean to you to be clothed in the righteousness of Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You do not leave me in my shame but provide a covering I could never make myself. Thank You that at the cost of Christ's own blood, I am clothed in His righteousness. Help me to stop trusting my fig leaves and rest fully in what You have provided. Amen.
